newsitem.title: KENYA: Bad weather lowers Kenya first quarter tea output.
newsitem.headline: Bad weather lowers Kenya first quarter tea output.

text.p: Kenya's tea production fell 37.03 percent in the first quarter of the year compared to 1996 partly on account of poor weather, a leading brokerage company said.
"Most (growing) areas remain wet but cold temperatures inhibit growth," Africa Tea Brokers (ATB) said in a statement on Wednesday. "Crop recovery from the prolonged drought is slow."
Drought in the December to early-March period had already undermined efforts to increase production and the brokerage company confirmed the drought effect had been devastating.
The brokers posted production in the January to March period at 44.05 million kg, a decrease of 25.9 million kg or 37.03 percent over that period last year.
They said production in the month of March was 6,221,175 kg, showing a drastic decrease of 16,826,643 kg or 73.01 percent over the same month last year.

Africa Tea Brokers said four sales were held during March when a total of 121,358 packages were sold at an average price of $1.99. Comparative figures for the same month last year were 272,476 packages sold at an average price of $1.41.
